outline: Adverse effects of drugs on the renal and urinary system
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis after gadolinium-based contrast exposure in advanced kidney failure
mechanism: Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis is a progressive fibrosing disorder associated with gadolinium-based contrast exposure in patients with markedly impaired renal function. Delayed elimination of gadolinium-based contrast in severe kidney disease is the key clinical risk context; the disorder produces symmetric hard or woody skin induration and may cause severe flexion contractures and disability.
vignette: A 59-year-old man with end-stage kidney disease receiving maintenance hemodialysis develops progressive tightening of the skin on both legs and forearms several weeks after a gadolinium-enhanced MRI. Examination shows symmetric brawny, indurated plaques with a hard, woody texture extending proximally from the distal extremities. Range of motion at the knees and elbows is reduced because of flexion contractures. The face is spared.
lead: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
distractor_notes: Calciphylaxis is strongly associated with end-stage renal disease, but it classically causes extremely painful ischemic skin lesions that may become violaceous, ulcerated, necrotic, or covered by eschar rather than symmetric woody fibrotic plaques with contractures after gadolinium exposure.

Diffuse cutaneous systemic sclerosis can cause widespread skin thickening and contractures, but the combination of advanced kidney failure, recent gadolinium-based contrast exposure, symmetric woody plaques beginning distally, and facial sparing is much more characteristic of nephrogenic systemic fibrosis.

Eosinophilic fasciitis can produce symmetric woody induration of the extremities and contractures, making it a plausible mimic, but it is not specifically linked to gadolinium exposure in advanced kidney failure and usually reflects eosinophilic inflammation of deep fascia.

Scleromyxedema is a scleroderma-like disorder typically associated with waxy papules and monoclonal gammopathy and commonly involves the face or neck, unlike the classic facial sparing of nephrogenic systemic fibrosis.
key_expl: This patient has nephrogenic systemic fibrosis. The decisive pattern is advanced kidney failure with recent gadolinium-based contrast exposure followed by symmetric, hard or woody induration of the extremities, progressive proximal spread, and flexion contractures with relative sparing of the face. Current gadolinium-based contrast labeling warns that nephrogenic systemic fibrosis occurs in patients with impaired elimination of these agents and may cause debilitating fibrosis of skin, muscle, and internal organs.
objective: Recognize nephrogenic systemic fibrosis as the characteristic diagnosis in a patient with severe renal impairment who develops symmetric woody skin induration and flexion contractures after gadolinium-based contrast exposure.
